question: does the animation in the committed bytes actually move on a current browser, and does it survive GitHub's own SVG viewer
browser: Chromium major version 151 (the UA's minor/build/patch are all zero; the dotted quad is not written out because infra/redact_scan.py reads one as an IPv4, and a version number is not a good enough reason to teach the scanner an exception) driven over CDP, prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference (asserted, not assumed)
read_from: the pushed blob served over http to rule out any local edit, and the same blob through GitHub's file view

the_gate_argument_is_itself_a_claim.finding: CSS.supports('offset-path', 'path("")') is FALSE in Chrome 151, while CSS.supports('offset-path', 'path("M 0 0 L 1 1")') is TRUE
the_gate_argument_is_itself_a_claim.why_it_matters: path("") is the idiomatic feature-detection spelling. A gate written that way closes on a browser that fully supports the feature; every dot then keeps its base opacity: 0, the diagram is silently static, and every offline check still passes because the gate is present and correctly nested.
the_gate_argument_is_itself_a_claim.now_checked_by: tests/test_architecture.py::animation_findings requires the @supports argument to be a quoted path beginning with a moveto; the named mutant is supports_argument_emptied

the_css_is_effective.conclusion: 3 of the first 4 dots change position between two driven timeline points, offset-distance sweeps 0% -> 100%, and opacity peaks at 1 inside each dot's window. The keyframes, the support gate and the offset-path all apply in Chrome 151.

what_this_pass_could_not_measure.problem: document.timeline.currentTime stayed 0 and every animation's currentTime stayed 0 across a 3 s wait, so the automation context does not advance the animation timeline at all
what_this_pass_could_not_measure.consequence: two viewport screenshots 2.5 s apart came back byte-identical (md5 ba1ba56eb748 both times). That is a measurement of the harness, not of the artifact — the same freeze would produce identical screenshots for any correct animation.
what_this_pass_could_not_measure.how_the_claim_was_rescued: the timeline was driven explicitly (Animation.currentTime set to fixed offsets) and positions read at each point. That proves the CSS produces motion; it does not prove a real viewer plays it.
what_this_pass_could_not_measure.still_manual: whether GitHub's own SVG viewer plays it. GitHub renders the file as inside viewscreen.githubusercontent.com, which is a separate origin, so nothing inside it can be inspected from the page. A human opening docs/architecture.svg on github.com is the only check for that, and it is listed in docs/test-design.md L5 rather than claimed here.
what_this_pass_could_not_measure.lesson: a probe proves nothing until it arrives: a frozen timeline and a broken animation are the same two screenshots.

degradation.no_offset_path_support: Firefox before 122, Safari before 16 — the @supports block never applies, .pkt/.dead keep the top-level opacity: 0, and the diagram is complete and static. The hop sequence is still readable as the numbered list, whose length is asserted equal to the dot list.
degradation.prefers_reduced_motion_reduce: same static diagram, by a second query
